name: emission-discipline
description: Emission Discipline (prose-may-hedge-fences-execute) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for WHAT the model is licensed to RELEASE into a code fence, and thus into user-owned systems. Models the experienced integration defect as (correct form available in-model) × (release layer that never checks the emission against it) — knowledge–emission divergence — and gates on what is about to be released, never on how casual the request was: eight defect classes by transmission vector (phantom reference, fossil, endorsed reject, unlanded fix, rhetorical laundering, label drift, scope breach, unconverged deferral), twenty-three rules in seven groups (mid-stream, turn-boundary, standing, mandate/license, session, delivery form — the final message after the turn's last tool call being the delivery surface, since the Code tab drops fences and widgets placed before the closing tool calls, the final message opening with a Deviations block that names every self-decided departure or says none — ask), a resident trigger table, a PreToolUse fence gate that asks before a persisted heredoc or written file carries a hedged literal, a deployment residency map recording that residency is not binding, and the two live case studies it was derived from and amended against. Consequential-side twin of verification-discipline: that framework gates what the model believes, this one gates what it releases. Ships the doctrine as a direct-invoke skill plus a resident-gate wrapper skill for user-level installs. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.
